# Board motion: coverage matrix

<!-- Generated by design/tools/board-motion-docs.mjs from design/board-motion/contract/ (coverage.json, cues.json, stations.json), the prototype fixtures and the prop-layer manifest. Do not edit by hand. -->

**A proposal, not owner-approved.** Issue [#87](https://github.com/Amirkianfar66/GameN/issues/87), board-motion-0.1.0. Design base `94a49ce0c5220b814ec56333b028fbe6180b257e` on `codex/v1-pass-board-targets` ([PR #86](https://github.com/Amirkianfar66/GameN/pull/86), unmerged): protocol 2, engine `full-game-1.1.0`, ruleset `in-person-v1-pass-2026-10-08`, Original Powers off. Tokens 0.4.0, assets `design-0.2.0` plus the prop layers `board-motion-0.1.0` (proposal).

Every action of the release is played on the comic board: chosen from a compact tray, its players picked by tapping their characters in their rooms, confirmed and answered in a strip above navigation. Moving is pressing a room's name; Pass is the middle of navigation. This page lists, for each of them, what the viewer's own view offers, how it is drawn, what is public and the cues that mark it; then every cue, the states every one of the nine characters has, the facts the board reads and where each comes from, the components and the runtime hooks they map onto, and the gaps. The reasoning and the integration steps are in [board-motion-handoff.md](board-motion-handoff.md); what was actually run is in [board-motion-verification.md](board-motion-verification.md).

Each scenario id opens in the prototype at `/board-motion/?scenario=<id>` on the design review server (`npm run dev:review --workspace @mothership/design-tokens`). Every name in it is synthetic.

## Every action with every character

An action's rules never look at a character: the view offers seats, and whichever character sits in an offered seat is drawn eligible by the same rules (the check holds the stylesheet to it: a rule keyed by a character sets only its picture). This table says, from the fixtures themselves, in which scenarios each character is offered or chosen for each action; the crowd scenarios put every character the rules allow within reach in one room. A dash is a combination the rules exclude, and the last column says which and why. The vocabulary sheet ([vocabulary.png](../../design/board-motion/review/vocabulary.png)) draws all nine in every state. In these fixtures the viewer is Player 3, character c1.

Pass names no one. Move names a room, never a character: the viewer's own piece is the one that moves, and every character's move is drawn by `cue-public-move` with its own lift and settle (below).

## The states of every character

The states every one of the nine characters has. They are drawn by the same rules for all nine: a character's picture never selects a rule, and nothing about a role or a faction changes any of them. What differs per character is public: its picture, and in a move its lift height and settle angle.

| State | Drawn | Cue |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `idle` | The standee (or the bust behind a prop) at its station, number and name on its stand. | none: a state, not a motion |
| `pressed-focused` | A focus outline on the 44 px press area; a light press tint while pressed. | none: a state, not a motion |
| `eligible` | Dashed caption-yellow ring at the base and a + tab; the others faint. | `cue-target-eligible` |
| `selected` | Lifted, solid ring, check stamp. | `cue-selection` |
| `multi-selected` | Solid ring and the pick's number. | `cue-target-pick` |
| `pending` | Dotted ring, ellipsis stamp; the strip's Sending stamp. | `cue-pending` |
| `accepted-registration` | The private marks are gone; the strip carries the Registered stamp. Nothing is drawn on the character. | `cue-registration` |
| `rejected-unavailable` | Faint, without a ring (not offered); a rejection is said in the strip with a hatched stamp, never on the character. | `cue-not-accepted` |
| `authoritative-movement` | Carried in an arc to its new station with an ink trail and a landing puff; its own lift and settle. | `cue-public-move` |
| `public-status-change` | A marker stamped on: Injured (leaning), Eliminated (grey, the revealed faction), Captain, Jailed. | `cue-status-change` |
| `active-turn` | The turn marker above the head. | `cue-turn-accent` |

The one public flourish that differs per character is in a move: how high it is lifted and how it settles (fixtures `CREW`, public, never a role).

| Character | Call sign | Lift (px) | Settle (deg) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `c1` | Vega | 6 | -3 |
| `c2` | Rigel | 4 | 2 |
| `c3` | Lyra | 8 | -2 |
| `c4` | Atlas | 3 | 1 |
| `c5` | Orion | 4 | -1 |
| `c6` | Nova | 7 | 3 |
| `c7` | Juno | 5 | -2 |
| `c8` | Mira | 6 | 2 |
| `c9` | Echo | 4 | -3 |

## Cues

The cues of the board-motion prototype (issue #87): every visible change it animates or marks, what starts it, who may see it, what fact it rests on, where it is drawn, how long, how it is cancelled, what stays when it ends, and what reduced motion shows instead. Six are the reviewed cues of design/contract/motion-cues.json, kept with their ids and durations; the rest are proposals of this work. None is owner-approved.

Rules every cue keeps:

- A cue adds no fact: what it marks is already on screen in words (a status line, a strip line, a tag, the readable list).
- A cue changes nothing and nothing waits for it: no health, resource, turn, phase, deadline or command depends on it. It is never queued.
- Public cues are started only by a change between two drawn public states (seats' location, health, jailed, captain, revealed faction; active seat; phase; round; the published tally). A replayed snapshot, a reconnect, a page that was in the background, and more than four moves in one update play no travel.
- Private cues are drawn only on the acting player's own board while their own action is open, from their own view's offers, their own taps and their own receipts. Closing, backgrounding, a stale view, time running out or a new phase removes them.
- No cue exists for a shot, a shooter, a weapon, an attack type, a block, Protection, a Rescue giver, a Supply giver, a Hack partner or any cause, on any surface. A health change is drawn the same whatever caused it.
- No cue has a sound, a vibration pattern, a light change in a room or a fetched picture. All pictures are in the bundles every device loads before the first view.
- Cue layers take no pointer events and cannot take focus. A newer authoritative state withdraws the cue in flight for the same seat; the latest state is what is drawn.
- Reduced motion: no travel, trail, shake, lift or zoom. Arrival, status changes, stamps and sheets use the 80 ms fade. The facts and the controls are the same.

| Cue | Status | Trigger | Audience and facts | Anchor | Timing | Cancelled by | Settled state | Reduced motion | Asset |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cue-tray-open`<br>interaction | proposal | The player presses Actions while nothing is in progress. | **local**. The actions the player's own view opens (legalTargets keys, availability flags). Nothing public. | `.bm-tray` | 220 ms (motionMs.cardTransition), --ms-ease-settle | Closing the tray, choosing an action, or any change that closes the private surface. | The tray is open over the lower board; the board stays visible above it. | 80 ms fade. | None: CSS panel. |

| `cue-tally`<br>game_event | proposal | A vote closes and the view carries lastTally. | **public**. The published aggregate counts and the selected seat. Never an individual ballot. | `.bm-piece__tally above each counted character` | 220 ms (motionMs.cardTransition), --ms-ease-standard | The next tally or phase that clears it. | A count label on each counted character; the selected one in caption yellow. | 80 ms fade. | None. |
| `cue-ballot-subject`<br>game_event | proposal | A release vote opens. | **public**. ballot.releaseTargetSeatId (public). | `.bm-piece[data-subject]` | none: a state | The vote closing. | A double ring and On the ballot on the jailed character. | The same. | None. |

Not produced, on purpose:

| What | Why |
| --- | --- |
| Any effect for a shot, Disable, Protection, Rescue, Hack, Scan, Supply or Code attempt on a public surface | Not authorized: no public event discloses an attacker, weapon, block, giver or cause (the view and event schemas of packages/contracts/src/full-game.ts). |
| A BANG, projectile, impact, heal or shield on a health change | PUBLIC_HEALTH_CHANGED says only the new health. Drawing a cause would invent a fact. |
| Sound and vibration | No audio asset exists; a sound or vibration per action would disclose private activity to anyone in earshot. |
| Idle loops, breathing, camera motion | Tokens say loops: false; nothing moves while nothing happens (DSN-D16). |

## Facts and where they come from

Every fact the board draws, the authorized source it is read from at the pinned tuple, who may see it and the cues that draw it. Nothing is drawn from anything else. A station (where in a room a character stands) is not a game fact: every device works it out the same way from public occupancy and seat order (design/board-motion/js/layout.js).

| Fact | Drawn | Source at the pinned tuple | Audience | Cues |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `seat-identity` | Each character's picture, seat number and name on its stand. | Lobby identity: seats[].characterId and seats[].displayName (packages/contracts/src/lobby-identity.ts), as the release's comic shell already reads them; seat numbers from seatId. | public | — |
| `location` | The room a character stands in, and its station there. | seats[].location in the public and player views (packages/contracts/src/full-game.ts); PUBLIC_MOVE events. | public | `cue-public-move` `layout-reflow` |
| `health` | Injured (leaning, marker) and Eliminated (grey, marker). | seats[].health; PUBLIC_HEALTH_CHANGED events (new health only, no cause). | public | `cue-status-change` |
| `jailed` | The Jailed marker. | seats[].jailed (views only: no event of its own; a change is seen as the difference between two views). | public | `cue-status-change` |
| `captain` | The Captain marker. | seats[].captain (views only). | public | `cue-status-change` |
| `revealed-faction` | The faction label on an Eliminated character. | seats[].revealedFaction, which the contract sets only for Eliminated seats before the end. | public | `cue-status-change` |
| `active-seat` | The turn marker over the active character; the status bar's words. | activeSeatId. | public | `cue-turn-accent` `cue-phase-change` |
| `phase` | The status bar's phase words and timer. | phase.kind, phase.endsAt; PHASE_CHANGED events. | public | `cue-phase-change` |
| `round` | The round chip. | round. | public | `cue-round-transition` |
| `release-subject` | On the ballot, over the jailed character a release vote is on. | ballot.releaseTargetSeatId. | public | `cue-ballot-subject` |
| `tally` | The published count over each counted character, the selected one in caption yellow. | lastTally (counts, selectedSeatId, yesCount, released). | public | `cue-tally` |
| `offers` | The tray's actions, the eligible characters, the room tags a move may use (after a press), Pass's availability. | The player's own view: legalTargets, self.*Available flags, self.movementDestinations, self.releaseVoteAvailable, legalTargets.PASS_TURN; the release's pending-command gate (ownPendingCommandIds and the controller's own request). | private | `cue-tray-open` `cue-target-eligible` `cue-move-tentative` |
| `own-choice` | Selected and numbered characters, the tentative place of a move, the strip's question and confirmation. | The player's own taps on their own device, before anything is sent. | local | `cue-selection` `cue-target-pick` `cue-strip-enter` `cue-room-press` |
| `receipt` | Sending, Registered, Not accepted, Unknown, in the strip. | The command receipt (accepted REGISTERED; rejected PHASE_CLOSED or NOT_ALLOWED), safe failures, and the player's own COMMAND_REGISTERED event. | private | `cue-pending` `cue-registration` `cue-not-accepted` `cue-unknown` |
| `card` | Role, held device, knowledge, own ballot, Hack partner, inside the Card only. | self.role, knowledge, ownBallot, hackPartnerSeatId of the player's own view. | private | `cue-sheet-open` |

## Rooms and stations

Every room has a hand-placed formation for each count from one to five occupants, in the places the reference page puts people (behind the chart table, at a console, in the bed, on the bench); six to nine in one room stand in a 3 x 3 crowd. A station is worked out on every device from public occupancy and seat order (`design/board-motion/js/layout.js`), so every screen draws the same. No capacity is implied: see GAP-2.

## Gaps and open decisions

What this design needs that the pinned tuple does not provide, and what it deliberately does not draw. None is a contract change made here: Integration owns the contracts.

| Id | Kind | What | In this design |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GAP-1 | none needed | Jailed, Captain and revealed-faction changes have no event of their own. | Draw them from the difference between two drawn views, as the release's director does for health and location. No contract change is proposed. |
| GAP-2 | owner decision | The owner's reference asks for at most five players in a room. The rules have no room capacity: rules/overlays/location-board-layout-v1.json says "Unnumbered token areas avoid imposing an artificial room-capacity rule", docs/design/art-direction.md asks for room for all nine without implying capacity, and docs/balance/rules-audit.md finds no capacity rule. | A hand-placed formation for each count from one to five in every room, and a 3 x 3 crowd formation when six to nine are in one room. A capacity would be a rule change for the game owner and Balance; the design works either way. |
| GAP-3 | owner decision | The reference draws arrows and lights along a corridor between rooms. The rules give no adjacency: rules/overlays/location-board-layout-v1.json says its dotted paths "illustrate possible Captain access, not a finalized adjacency decision". | A steel spine with four lamps between the columns, no arrow, door or path. |
| GAP-4 | owner decision | Room subtitles (Captain, Engineering, Laboratory) come from the reference, not from the rules or the release. | Proposed words, aria-hidden; the room's name is what is read and pressed. |
| GAP-5 | asset | The three prop layers (Command Room table, Room B counter, Hospital bed) are not in the reviewed manifest design-0.2.0. | Generated from the approved sources as a versioned proposal (board-motion-0.1.0); adopted only through an Integration review of a later manifest revision. |
| GAP-6 | asset | The Final Zone has no picture of its own in the reviewed kit. | The page's paper ground with the approved halftone and speed lines. A picture is a later asset decision. |
